title: Gaussian limit for Lipschitz functions of cube sums
statement: Let $c\ge0$ and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $c$-Lipschitz. For each positive integer $m$, choose a uniformly random vector $X\in\{0,1\}^{m+1}$ and encode each coordinate by $1$ for $0$ and $-1$ for $1$. The expectation of $\psi$ applied to the sum of these signs divided by $\sqrt{m+1}$ tends, as $m\to\infty$, to the expectation of $\psi$ under the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R$.
replaced: For every $c\ge0$ and $c$-Lipschitz $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $2^{-(m+1)}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{m+1}}\psi((m+1)^{-1/2}\sum_i(-1)^{x_i})\to\mathbb E\psi(Z)$ as $m\to\infty$, where $Z$ is standard Gaussian.
